topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning objectives of the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the fundamental concepts of cancer development, exploring the relative roles of endogenous mutations, genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, using the relationship between malaria, Epstein-Barr virus, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how physical agents and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing in the body to produce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the multi-stage model of tumor promotion, host developmental timing, and a synthesis of carcinogenic pathways.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their associated risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary slide of the lecture.
